samples.summary: The test claiming to cover the new freeze-snap inside `shiftCells` never triggers the snap
samples.evidence: `it('should keep the freeze clear of a block when rows are inserted')` merges A2:A4, calls setFreezePane(2,0) (already snapped to 4 by `setFreezePane`), then `insertRows(1, 1)`. In `shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1392-1417) the pre-existing branch `count > 0 && index <= frozen` already yields frozenRows = 5, and the shifted block A3:A5 satisfies range[1].r (5) > rows (5) === false, so `snapFreezePastMerges` at sheet.ts:1422 makes no change. The asserted `{ frozenRows: 5, frozenCols: 0 }` holds identically with the whole new snap block deleted — it is fake coverage for that block. No test in the diff or in packages/sheets/test/sheet/freeze-pane.test.ts drives a structural edit that actually leaves a block straddling the boundary (e.g. deleting rows inside the frozen area so a block ends up half-frozen, or inserting rows inside a block that sits on the boundary), which is exactly the state the new code exists to prevent.

samples.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` column axis and its cascading multi-pass loop are untested
samples.evidence: Only the row axis is exercised: 'should snap the freeze past a block it would cut in half' uses setFreezePane(2, 0) and a vertical block. No test sets frozenCols with a horizontal merged block (the `cols > 0 && range[0].c <= cols && range[1].c > cols` branch, sheet.ts), and no test has two blocks where snapping one boundary pulls a second block across it — the case the `while (changed)` loop exists for. A bug in either branch silently leaves an undrawable straddling block.
searchedFor: merge.test.ts 'Sheet merge and the freeze boundary' describe

samples.summary: Merge deletions performed by a paste are never asserted against the store, only against the in-memory map
samples.evidence: 'should persist the pasted merge to the store' checks `store.getMerges().get('A3')` for the created block, but every test of the delete side ('should drop a destination block the paste fully covers', 'should drop a cut merged block at the source') asserts only `sheet.getMerges()`. `applyPasteMerges` calls `this.store.deleteMerge(...)` alongside `this.merges.delete(...)`; if the store call were dropped the in-memory assertions still pass and the merge would resurrect on reload — a persisted-data defect.
searchedFor: new copy-paste describe block in the diff

samples.summary: The spill-cleanup branches of the newly extracted `clearCellsUnderMerge` are untested on the paste path (and on the move path)
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` handles spill anchors (deleting ghosts), `spillBlocked` cells and `unblockedAnchors` re-spill, and `paste` now feeds `unblockedAnchors` into the recalculation. `grep -l spill packages/sheets/test` returns only worksheet-grid, calculation, data-validation, formatting, style-mutation and formula tests — none of merge.test.ts, moving.test.ts or clipboard.test.ts. So no test pastes/moves a merged block over a spill anchor or a blocked anchor; orphaned ghost cells or a spill that never re-attempts would ship undetected.

samples.summary: `snapshotMergesIn`'s exclusion of partially-clipped blocks has no test
samples.evidence: `snapshotMergesIn` filters `getMergesIntersecting(range)` with `isRangeInRange(m.range, range)`, so a block the copy range only clips is deliberately omitted from the copy buffer. No test in the new 'Sheet merge + copy-paste' block copies a range that clips a block (all copies either contain the block whole or avoid it), so removing the filter — which would re-create a truncated/overlapping block at the destination — would not fail any test.
searchedFor: new copy-paste describe block in merge.test.ts

samples.summary: The HTML (spreadsheet-HTML) paste branch of `normalizeSingleCellGrid` is untested
samples.evidence: 'should paste an external grid from the anchor too' and 'should not shift a multi-cell external paste off the selected row' both go through the plain-TSV branch (`paste({ text: ... })`). The `html2grid` branch also wraps its result in `normalizeSingleCellGrid`, and no test passes `{ html }` with a single cell onto a merge-covered active cell. A regression there would silently hide the pasted value under the block.

samples.summary: The removal of `clearCopyBuffer()` from the two view paste handlers has no test at either view
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4941 and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:724 both dropped `this.sheet.clearCopyBuffer()` after `paste`. The model-level consequence is covered ('should propagate merges on a second paste from the same copy'), but nothing exercises the view handlers themselves, so re-introducing the clear in either handler — which would demote every repeat paste to external again — would not fail any test. grep for clearCopyBuffer in packages/sheets/test finds only clipboard.test.ts:357 (a direct model call).

In 'should drop the copy buffer when rows are reordered', `expect(text).toBe('10')` merely re-asserts the value written by `setData` and is true regardless of the move-clears-buffer behavior under test. The meaningful assertion (`getCopyRange()` undefined) is present, so this is cosmetic only.

samples.summary: The three new `RangeOpRefusal` message strings have no test
samples.evidence: `refusalMessage` in packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts gained 'merge-paste-partial', 'merge-paste-frozen' and 'merge-move-frozen' cases; grep for refusalMessage across packages/sheets finds it only in src/view/worksheet.ts — there is no test file for it (the sheet tests assert the refusal codes, not the strings). Impact is a wrong user-facing string only.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. In merge.test.ts:815-830 the test merges A2:A4, setFreezePane(2,0) snaps to 4 (sheet.ts:536-560), then insertRows(1,1) hits the PRE-EXISTING branch in shiftCells (sheet.ts:1396-1403: count>0 && index=1<=frozen=4 → frozenRows=5). The shifted block is A3:A5, so snapFreezePastMerges(5,0) at sheet.ts:1422-1427 evaluates range[0].r=3<=5 && range[1].r=5>5 → false and changes nothing. The asserted {frozenRows:5, frozenCols:0} (line 829) therefore holds identically with the new snap block deleted — it is not coverage for that block. I also read freeze-pane.test.ts in full (1-196): its insert/delete tests (43-111) use no merges at all, and only merge.test.ts and freeze-pane.test.ts call setFreezePane, so nothing in the suite drives a structural edit that actually leaves a block straddling the boundary. I considered refuting on unreachability of the new snap path, but could not establish that from shiftMergeMap/moveRows semantics, and speculative unreachability is not a valid named ground. Gap is major: failure of the untested snap leaves an undrawable half-frozen merged block (user-visible rendering corruption).
